small_guidance:
- The inner reduction loads a [BLOCK_N] x vector and a [BLOCK_OC] w vector per (ic,kh,kw) and does an outer product accumulate — convert this into a proper GEMM by tiling along K (IC*KH*KW) with a BLOCK_K (e.g. 16/32) and using `tl.dot` on [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_OC] tiles; this exploits tensor cores and should give a large step on the 4090.
- Add autotune configs that increase BLOCK_N up to 128/256 with BLOCK_OC=64 (OC=64 so one OC tile covers all channels), drop the pid_oc grid dimension when OC fits a single tile, and try num_stages=3-4 to better hide global-memory latency on the K loop.
- Cache the per-row (b, oh, ow) index math once outside the loop (already done) but also hoist `b*stride_xb` and precompute per-kh row base pointers to reduce address arithmetic in the hottest loop.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM conv: collapse (ic, kh, kw) into a K dimension of size IC*KH*KW=72, tile M=output spatial positions (BLOCK_M=64/128), N=OC (BLOCK_N=64), K (BLOCK_K=32 or full 72 in static_range), and use `tl.dot` so the MAC pipeline hits tensor cores instead of scalar FMAs.
- Use NHWC (channels-last) layout for x and y so the K-dim (ic) is contiguous, enabling vectorized loads along K; permute the weight to [OC, KH, KW, IC] at init for the same reason.
- Fuse bias + ReLU + HardSwish in the epilogue on the accumulator (already done) and consider one program per (N tile, OC tile) with persistent loops over the small KH*KW=9 to keep the K loop fully unrolled via `tl.static_range`.
